title: SIG/CAIQ runbook + pricing impact analysis for enterprise attestations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Create an operational runbook and templated artifacts for responding to SIG/CAIQ and common enterprise security questionnaires, and evaluate how different levels of attestation/response packaging affect pricing/packaging experiments and sales cycle duration.

Scope:
- Produce a living runbook that maps SIG/CAIQ controls to Redwood product features, support obligations, and required evidence (logs, architecture diagrams, third-party attestations).
- Build a set of customer-facing attestations: a short "security snapshot" (one-page) for renewals and a detailed CAIQ response package for due diligence.
- Define three packaging tiers (Self-Serve, Assisted Attestation, Premium Attestation SLA) and run a pricing experiment to measure willingness-to-pay and impact on deal velocity.
- Integrate attestation status into Console metadata (customer profile) and Sales collateral.

Deliverables:
1) SIG/CAIQ Runbook (master mapping + checklist)
2) CAIQ response template with sample evidence links (redacted)
3) One-page Customer Security Snapshot PDF template
4) Pricing experiment design doc and A/B config for sales-led offers
5) Console flag for attestation status (UI spec + event to surface in account overview)
6) Legal/Privacy review and standard redline guidance for customers

Risks & constraints:
- Some evidence requires engineering time to extract (audit logs, egress attestations) — may push timeline.
- Legal sign-off for an "attestation SLA" could require additional insurance and SLO definitions.
- Pricing signals may vary significantly by industry; experiments must segment by vertical and ARR band.

Primary stakeholders: PM (Aisha Patel), Security/Trust (Marco Ruiz), Legal (Renee Cho), Sales Ops (Diego Alvarez), Console Eng (Priya Nair).
activity_log: 2025-02-18 - Aisha Patel: Ticket created after sales flagged longer-than-expected DD for three RFPs; outlined scope and initial deliverables.
2025-02-20 - Marco Ruiz: Security reviewed initial SIG/CAIQ mapping; called out 12 controls that require new log exports (auth events, KV cache access patterns). Added to dependencies.
2025-02-24 - Priya Nair: Console engineering scoped a UI badge to show 'Attestation Status' and an API endpoint to fetch the one-page snapshot. Estimate 3 points frontend + 2 backend.
2025-02-28 - Renee Cho (Legal): Requested standard disclaimer language and a draft redline for the Premium Attestation SLA; flagged potential insurance requirements.

2025-03-03 - Aisha Patel: Pricing experiment design v1 completed - A/B variants (no attestation, paid Assisted Attestation, included in Enterprise) and success metrics (deal velocity, conversion rate, average contract value).
2025-03-05 - Diego Alvarez (Sales Ops): Agreed to run pilot with three AE teams in North America; added segmentation by ARR (<250k, 250k-2M, >2M).
notes: Decision: Start with a Minimal Viable Attestation (MVA) package that covers top 20 SIG controls for Sales; escalate to full CAIQ when requested.
Trade-off: Building automated evidence exports reduces manual work but costs ~2 sprints. Consider short-term manual redaction process for low ARR deals.
Follow-up: Security to provide sample redacted logs by 2025-03-10. Engineering to confirm API contract for snapshot by 2025-03-14.
Review feedback: Sales asked that the one-page snapshot include 'time-to-respond' estimate for full CAIQ (target <= 5 business days for Assisted Attestation).
